Topic Area 5 – Solvent Targeted Recovery and Precipitation (STRAP) of Plastic Wastes Task 2.5: Development of STRAP process for rigid PIW films focused on the development of computational and experimental methods to apply STRAP to rigid post-industrial waste (PIW) films. We developed a computational method for rapidly predicting polymer solubilities by performing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to generate oligomer conformations which are then input to density functional theory and COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Real Solvents (COSMO-RS) calculations to compute solubilities. To capture the impact of crystallinity, solubilities were computed using a solid-liquid equilibrium approach in which the degree of crystallinity influences the heat of fusion. We formulated a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model to identify solvents and temperatures for the selective dissolution of target polymers based on these computed solubilities. Milestone 2.5.1: Design solvent compositions and processing temperatures for the selective dissolution of 7 different polymers (PE, PP, PET, EVOH, Nylon, PS and PVC) that are common in rigid and flexible multilayer films with computational approach to predict solubility as a function of crystallinity was met using this approach. Using these computational data, we selected representative “good” and “poor” solvents for each of these polymers and corresponding solubilities were experimentally measured at multiple temperatures for comparison to computational predictions. These data indicated good agreement between simulations and experiments (within ~5 wt%) for most polymer-solvent combinations, with PS yielding larger, yet qualitatively correct, predictions and PET yielding qualitatively incorrect results, which we attributed to kinetic factors. These results met Milestone 2.5.2: Measure solubility of 7 different polymers (PE, PP, PET, EVOH, Nylon, PS and PVC) that are common in rigid and flexible multilayer films as a function of crystallinity and temperature to compare with computational predictions. The combined computational and experimental data were used to create a solubility database with 7 polymers (eventually expanded to 11) and over 1000+ solvents. To meet Milestone 2.5.3: Recover >90 wt% of each component of physical mixtures containing up to 5 polymer components to mimic rigid film compositions using solvents designed computationally and measure resulting properties, computational and experimental efforts focused on achieving the separation of physical mixtures of polymer components. We used the solubility database to determine suggested solvents for the separation of physical mixtures. The workflow for this approach is summarized in Figure 5.1. Three physical mixtures were considered, all involving common polymer components of multilayer films: polyethylene (PE) and polystyrene (PS); PE and polyvinylchloride (PVC); and polypropylene, ethylene vinyl alcohol (EVOH), polyethylene terephthalate (PET). We also considered two different sequences for the separation of PE/PS vs. PS/PE which differed in the component that was solubilized. Table 5.1 summarizes the wt% recovery of each sample; >90 wt% recovery is obtained in each case. An even larger number of components (up to 10) was also studied using a similar approach (Sanchez- Rivera et al, Waste Manag, 2025).
